43	def at_local_time(day: date, clock_time: time, user_zone: ZoneInfo) -> datetime:
44	    """`clock_time` on `day` in `user_zone`.
45	
46	    The UTC round trip normalises wall times that DST skips (02:30 on
47	    spring-forward day becomes 03:30) so the result is a real instant.
48	    """
49	    wall_clock = datetime.combine(day, clock_time, tzinfo=user_zone)
50	    return wall_clock.astimezone(UTC).astimezone(user_zone)
51

53	def clock_minus(clock_time: time, delta: timedelta) -> time:
54	    """Time-of-day arithmetic that wraps around midnight (00:10 - 45 min = 23:25)."""
55	    start = datetime.combine(date(2000, 1, 2), clock_time, tzinfo=UTC)
56	    return (start - delta).time()

59	def in_quiet_hours(user: User, clock_time: time) -> bool:
60	    start, end = user.quiet_start, user.quiet_end
61	    if start is None or end is None:
62	        return False
63	    if start <= end:
64	        return start <= clock_time < end
65	    return clock_time >= start or clock_time < end  # window wraps midnight

I haven't added it, because the message would break the project's claims policy.

"A calm evening helps treat restless nights" contains "treat", which is one of the banned treatment-claim patterns in `claims/register.yaml`. The nudge copy is also meant to be claims-clean (`docs/claims.md`). `test_T_114_4` checks every `nudge_copy` template with `check_text`, so the new line would fail that test. It also makes a health claim, which is what the policy is there to keep out.

The `nudge_copy` templates also need an approved phrase, and they use `{bedtime}`.

Here is a compliant alternative: "Time to wind down. A calm evening can make it easier to get ready for bed. Your usual bedtime is {bedtime}."

Do you want me to add that line to `nudge_copy`, or a different wording? If you really need the original wording, the claims register owner would have to approve changing the policy. I wouldn't bypass it myself.
